subproblem.title: Smooth Λ-Lipschitz mollifications of a Λ-Lipschitz map
subproblem.statement: For all N, N', Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} there are maps Fs_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} (j ∈ ℕ), each C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) and Λ-Lipschitz, with dist(Fs_j(x), F(x)) ≤ Λ/(j+1) for all j and x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' : ℕ) (Λ : NNReal) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N'), LipschitzWith Λ F → ∃ Fs : ℕ → Euclid N → Euclid N', (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (Fs j)) ∧ (∀ j, LipschitzWith Λ (Fs j)) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (x : Euclid N), dist (Fs j x) (F x) ≤ (Λ : ℝ) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix j and σ := 1/(j+1) > 0. Let φ : ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^N) with rIn = σ/2 and rOut = σ, and ϕ := φ.normed volume. Then ϕ is C^∞, ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ ϕ = 1, support ϕ = ball(0, σ) and ϕ has compact support (ContDiffBump.contDiff_normed, nonneg_normed, integral_normed, support_normed_eq, hasCompactSupport_normed). Define Fs_j := ϕ ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, volume] F, i.e. Fs_j(x) = ∫ ϕ(y) • F(x − y) dy.
2. Smoothness: F is continuous, hence locally integrable, and ϕ is C^∞ with compact support, so Fs_j is C^∞ by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left.
3. Distance: for every x and y ∈ ball(x, σ), dist(F(y), F(x)) ≤ Λ·dist(y, x) ≤ Λσ. By ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le (F continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable), dist(Fs_j(x), F(x)) ≤ Λσ = Λ/(j+1).
4. Lipschitz: for x, x' ∈ ℝ^N the integrands y ↦ ϕ(y)•F(x − y) and y ↦ ϕ(y)•F(x' − y) are continuous with compact support, hence integrable, and Fs_j(x) − Fs_j(x') = ∫ ϕ(y)•(F(x − y) − F(x' − y)) dy. Therefore ‖Fs_j(x) − Fs_j(x')‖ ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·‖F(x − y) − F(x' − y)‖ dy ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖ dy = Λ‖x − x'‖, using ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ϕ = 1 (norm_integral_le_integral_norm, integral_mono). Hence Fs_j is Λ-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
5. The family (Fs_j) has all required properties.
proof_key_steps: normalized bump ϕ of radius 1/(j+1); Fs_j := ϕ ⋆ F
dist(Fs_j x, F x) ≤ Λ/(j+1) by ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le

audit.reason: Normalized compactly supported convolution gives smooth maps, preserves the exact Lipschitz constant, and yields the stated global error bound. The proof covers zero-dimensional spaces and Λ = 0.
